title: Claims Recovery Accounting: Measuring the Liability Restated on Lines Paid for Days Outside Cover
content:
This is the accounting basis on which the liability restated on a policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies is measured. What is restated is the recorded liability of the lines that fall outside cover, less what the coverage that was in force on those days leaves the policyholder and less what has already been taken back.

**Finding the lines.** The lines that fall outside cover are found by comparing the date of service of each paid line with the day the policy took effect. No line is found outside cover, the policy having been in force for every day its paid lines fall on.

**Which of them are restated.** Every line that falls outside cover is restated.

**The liability of the lines restated.** The liability of the lines restated is measured from the record. Nothing is taken as the liability of those lines.

**What stays with the policyholder.** The policyholder is left nothing, and the whole of the liability is restated.

**Applying what is left with the policyholder.** What is left with the policyholder is not applied at all, no line falling outside cover.

**What has already come back.** Nothing already taken back is deducted.

**The figure.** The liability of the lines restated is reduced by what is left with the policyholder and by what has already been taken back, the figure is rounded to the cent once at the end, and where those reductions exceed the liability nothing is restated.

### Worked through on hypothetical figures

Take a policy whose claim record carries three paid crossover lines, each recording the policyholder owing 40.00, and which took effect before the earliest of their dates of service.

Comparing each date of service with the day the policy took effect, no line is found outside cover. Every line that falls outside cover is restated, and there are none. Nothing is taken as the liability of those lines, so the liability measured is 0.00. The policyholder is left nothing. What is left with the policyholder is not applied at all. Nothing already taken back is deducted.

Reducing a liability of 0.00 by nothing and by nothing leaves 0.00, and rounded to the cent once at the end the liability restated is 0.00.
